common_name: Yankee Doodle Mountain Laurel (Vigorous Maroon-Banded Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Yankee Doodle is an upright, vigorous, disease-resistant selection that grows quickly to 8-10 feet.

directions: Site in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; Yankee Doodle is an upright, vigorous, densely branched selection with leaf-spot-resistant dark green foliage. Vivid pinkish-red buds open in late spring to a near-white corolla banded with a narrow burgundy-maroon ring, produced abundantly on a quick-growing, semi-compact shrub. Its dense branching and disease resistance make it a strong hedge or specimen selection where a larger-scale mountain laurel is wanted. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Tiddlywinks Mountain Laurel (Dwarf Compact Pink-Budded Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun; Tiddlywinks is a slow, dwarf, compact selection reaching only about 3 feet after a decade.

directions: Site in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to partial sun, where Tiddlywinks forms a dense, compact dome reaching only about 3 feet after a decade, roughly half the size of the species. Dark pink buds open to pale, ballet-skirt-like pink flowers in late spring to early summer, set off by half-sized dark green leaves and red stems. Its small stature suits foundation plantings, rock gardens, and smaller shade borders where full-sized mountain laurel would overwhelm the space. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Kaleidoscope Mountain Laurel (Sarah x Bullseye Banded Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; avoid soggy sites and heavy afternoon sun. Kaleidoscope was bred by Richard Jaynes from a cross of 'Sarah' and 'Bullseye'.

directions: Site in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in dappled or part shade. Bred by Richard Jaynes at Broken Arrow Nursery from a cross of 'Sarah' and 'Bullseye', Kaleidoscope is a vigorous, well-branched, wide-upright selection with reddish new growth. Brilliant red buds open late in the season to a broad cinnamon-red band that nearly fills the white corolla, a bold patterned effect among the most eye-catching of the banded mountain laurel cultivars. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Heart of Fire Mountain Laurel (Ostbo Red Seedling Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Heart of Fire was selected as a seedling of 'Ostbo Red' for its rich red buds.

directions: Site in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade. Selected as a seedling of 'Ostbo Red', Heart of Fire bears red buds that open to deep pink flowers held in large corymbs from late spring into early summer, above glossy, dark green evergreen foliage. Reaching about 4 to 6 feet tall, it offers some of the richest bud color among widely grown mountain laurel selections. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Pink Charm Mountain Laurel (Deep Pink Ringed Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Pink Charm bears deep pink buds and rich pink, dark-ringed flowers on a 5-8 foot shrub.

directions: Site in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun. Pink Charm bears deep pink, angular buds that open to rich pink flowers marked with a narrow dark pink ring near the base of the corolla, carried in large clusters at the branch tips from late May into June above glossy green foliage and purplish-red stems. Growing 5 to 8 feet tall and wide, it is attractive to bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds and resists deer browsing. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Bay State Mountain Laurel (Salmon-Pink Crimped-Flower Selection)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade, keeping soil reliably moist in sunnier spots; Bay State bears crimped salmon-pink flowers.

directions: Site in acidic, moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade, keeping soil reliably moist if grown in sunnier spots. Bay State is a dense, bushy, leaf-spot-resistant selection with glossy, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Reddish-pink buds open from late spring to midsummer into large, dome-shaped flowerheads of distinctively crimped, cup-shaped salmon-to-coral-pink flowers. Like all mountain laurel, every part of the plant is toxic if ingested.

common_name: Funky Flow Mahonia (Neon Yellow Winter-Flowering Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Funky Flow is an NC State-bred hybrid of 'Winter Sun' and 'Soft Caress' with neon-yellow winter flowers.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, though plants also tolerate more sun than most mahonias. Bred at North Carolina State University from a cross of Mahonia x media 'Winter Sun' and Mahonia 'Soft Caress', this compact, dense, mounded hybrid grows to about 4 feet tall and wide with semi-evergreen dark green foliage. Vivid, neon-yellow flower spikes open from late fall through winter, providing fragrant color and pollinator interest during the dormant season, followed by ornamental fruit. It tolerates dry shade and is noted for resisting black walnut toxicity, making it useful near black walnut trees where many shrubs fail.

common_name: Groovy Glow Mahonia (Multicolor Flame-Spike Winter Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist but well-drained soil in part to full shade; Groovy Glow is an NC State-bred hybrid from the 'Winter Sun' x 'Soft Caress' line with multicolor flower spikes.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist but well-drained soil in part to full shade, though established plants also tolerate full sun. Bred at North Carolina State University from an open-pollinated seedling in the same 'Winter Sun' x 'Soft Caress' breeding line, this hybrid produces dark to medium green, fern-like, bamboo-textured evergreen foliage that flushes burgundy-bronze in spring. From late fall into early winter it bears dense, candle-like flower spikes in an unusual mix of yellow, orange, and red on the same spike, followed by blue-black berries. Reaching 3 to 4 feet tall and 4 to 6 feet wide, it is a distinctive multicolor-flowered addition to the shade border.

common_name: King's Ransom Mahonia (Hybrid Oregon Grape with Bronze Winter Foliage)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; King's Ransom is an upright hybrid Oregon grape prized for bluish-green foliage that turns bronze-red in winter.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade, where King's Ransom forms an upright-mounded hybrid Oregon grape with spiny, holly-shaped, bluish-green evergreen leaves that emerge burgundy in spring and turn bronze-red through winter. Showy, fragrant racemes of yellow flowers hang below the branches in early spring, followed by an abundant crop of attractive blue, grape-like berries from midsummer into fall that draw birds. Slow-growing and long-lived, it makes a durable specimen or background shrub for a shaded border. Prune only to remove dead or leggy canes at the base.

common_name: Sweet and Lo Sweet Box (Jasmine-Scented Proven Winners Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, acidic soil in part to full shade; a Proven Winners ColorChoice introduction with a compact, mounded, lightly suckering habit.

directions: Site in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained, acidic soil in part shade to full shade, where Sweet and Lo tolerates as little as a few hours of direct sun per day. This Proven Winners ColorChoice introduction forms a compact, mounded, lightly suckering evergreen shrub, useful as a fragrant groundcover beneath trees or along shaded walks. From late winter into early spring it bears small, two-toned hot-pink-and-white flowers with a sweet, jasmine-like fragrance carried on old wood, followed by black berries. It attracts bees and butterflies, resists deer, and needs only minimal pruning to remove dead or wayward stems.
